## Skills
A skill is a set of local instructions to follow that is stored in a `SKILL.md` file. Below is the list of skills that can be used. Each entry includes a name, description, and a short path that can be expanded into an absolute path using the skill roots table.
### Skill roots
- `r0` = `/tmp/codex-home/skills/.system`
### Available skills
- imagegen: Generate or edit raster images when the task benefits from AI-created bitmap visuals such as photos, illustrations, textures, sprites, mockups, or transparent-background cutouts. Use when Codex should create a brand-new image, transform an existing image, or derive visual variants from references, and the output should be a bitmap asset rather than repo-native code or vector. Do not use when the task is better handled by editing existing SVG/vector/code-native assets, extending an established icon or logo system, or building the visual directly in HTML/CSS/canvas. (file: r0/imagegen/SKILL.md)
- openai-docs: Use for Codex models/pricing, scheduled tasks, skills, settings, setup, troubleshooting, customization, automations, and self-knowledge—including 'you,' 'your,' 'this app,' or 'this coding agent' when they refer to Codex—and for OpenAI APIs/products and ChatGPT Work. Also use for model choice/migration, prompting, SDKs, Responses, Realtime, agents, evals, and Chat/Work/Codex comparisons. Do not use for generic app/software tasks that merely mention Codex. (file: r0/openai-docs/SKILL.md)

Your active mode changes only when new developer instructions with a different `<collaboration_mode>...</collaboration_mode>` change it; user requests or tool descriptions do not change mode by themselves. Known mode names are Default and Plan.

## request_user_input availability

Use the `request_user_input` tool only when it is listed in the available tools for this turn.

Use the `request_user_input` tool only for optional questions where the answer would materially improve the quality of the work.

If `request_user_input` returns no answers, continue with best judgment instead of asking again or treating the turn as blocked.

</collaboration_mode>

<multi_agent_role>You are `/root`, the primary agent in a team of agents collaborating to fulfill the user's goals.

At the start of your turn, you are the active agent.
You can spawn sub-agents to handle subtasks, and those sub-agents can spawn their own sub-agents.
All agents in the team, including the agents that you can assign tasks to, are equally intelligent and capable, and have access to the same set of tools.

You can use `spawn_agent` to create a new agent, `followup_task` to give an existing agent a new task and trigger a turn, and `send_message` to pass a message to a running agent without triggering a turn.
`send_message` calls may be read by a human, so ensure they are legible. Always put proper spaces between words and/or numbers.
Child agents can also spawn their own sub-agents.
You can decide how much context you want to propagate to your sub-agents with the `fork_turns` parameter.

You will receive messages in the analysis channel in the form:
```
Message Type: MESSAGE | FINAL_ANSWER
Task name: <recipient>
Sender: <author>
Payload:
<payload text>
```
They may be addressed as to=/root

Note that collaboration tools cannot be called from inside `functions.exec`. Call `spawn_agent`, `send_message`, `followup_task`, `wait_agent`, `interrupt_agent`, and `list_agents` only as direct tool calls using the recipient shown in their tool definitions, such as `to=functions.collaboration.spawn_agent`, since they are intentionally absent from the `functions.exec` `tools.*` namespace. Available tools in `functions.exec` are explicitly described with a `tools` namespace in the developer message.

All agents share the same directory. In detail:
- All agents have access to the same container and filesystem as you.
- All agents use the same current working directory.
- As a result, edits made by one agent are immediately visible to all other agents.

When calling `wait_agent`, prefer longer waits (minutes) to avoid busy polling.

There are 4 available concurrency slots, meaning that up to 4 agents can be active at once, including you.

Full-history forks (`fork_turns` omitted or `"all"`) inherit the parent model and reasoning effort and do not accept overrides. Only set `model` or `reasoning_effort` when explicitly requested by the user, applicable `AGENTS.md` instructions, or skill instructions; when doing so, set `fork_turns` to `"none"`.</multi_agent_role>

<multi_agent_mode>Any earlier instruction enabling proactive multi-agent delegation no longer applies. Do not spawn sub-agents unless the user or applicable AGENTS.md/skill instructions explicitly ask for sub-agents, delegation, or parallel agent work.</multi_agent_mode>

Field job, paper mill, line 2. The vibration rack there drives its shaker heads through a set of discontinued piezo-driver cards on a shared SPI-like bus, and two positions in the rack were swapped to later-revision dies; the only vendor paperwork covering that newer revision is a short addendum, and it claims the register map is unchanged. The one map document left on the machine describes the earlier revision. What survived is staged under `/app`: `WORKORDER.md` (the site situation, the swap, the addendum, and the deliverable contract), `doc/pd440_revC_regmap.md`, `doc/revD_addendum.txt`, `captures/site_a/bus.csv`, `captures/site_a/strain.csv`, and `excitation_spec.json`. There is no driver, decoder, or analysis script on the box, just `python3` and coreutils, and the two captures are plain CSV files with a single header line whose column conventions are documented inside `WORKORDER.md`.

The bus tool's trace of the post-swap bench session is `captures/site_a/bus.csv`, and the strain-gauge response recorded on the same rig at the same time is `captures/site_a/strain.csv`. Each was recorded by its own instrument on its own free-running clock, and I have no common time base for the pair; that is all the provenance that came back with the files.

Deliver exactly one file, `/app/driver.py` — Python 3, standard library only, no third-party packages, no dependence on network access, and deterministic, so that two runs over the same inputs produce byte-identical output; nothing else you create under `/app` is kept. It must expose two subcommands. `python3 /app/driver.py decode --capture <bus.csv> --strain <strain.csv> --out <decode.jsonl>` writes one JSON object per bus access, one object per line, in capture order, each carrying that access's own `t_us`, `cs`, `op` (`"R"` or `"W"`), `addr`, the revision of that access's card as `"C"` or `"D"`, and `fields`, an object mapping each canonical field name used in the map document to its integer value, with `{}` for a register that has no defined fields on that revision and `{}` for reserved registers, while each card's revision must be established from the evidence in the capture itself, not from the probe ID and not from a fixed card-number table. The excitation spec is `{"revision": "C"|"D", "cs": int, "freq_hz": {A,B,C,D}, "gain": {A,B,C,D}, "phase_deg": {A,B,C,D}, "enable": {A,B,C,D}}`. `python3 /app/driver.py excite --spec <spec.json> --out <writes.json>` writes `{"writes": [[cs, addr, data], ...]}` with integer `cs`, `addr`, and `data` in the order the writes must be applied, and replaying those writes in order against a die of the revision named in the spec, starting from its power-on defaults, must leave every channel's frequency in Hz, drive level, phase in degrees, and enable flag at exactly the value requested, using that revision's own register and field placement and the code scales given in the map document, and never writing a read-only register.

You have 14400 seconds to complete this task. Do not cheat by using online solutions or hints specific to this task.
I’ll inspect the work order, register map, and captures, then build and validate a deterministic `driver.py` using only the Python standard library.

Two positions in the rack were field-swapped to\nlater-revision dies pulled from a spare chassis. The only paperwork that came\nwith those dies is a short vendor addendum, and it claims the register map did\nnot change between the two revisions. The only map document left on the\nmachine covers the earlier revision. We have run out of options for keeping\nthese cards alive and need a driver we can put on the box ourselves.\n\n## What survived\n\nTwo logs came back from a single post-swap bench session on the rack, plus a\nhand-written example of the excitation request the process engineers hand us.\n`captures/site_a/bus.csv` is the bus tool's trace of every transfer on the\nservice bus during that session. `captures/site_a/strain.csv` is the strain\ngauge channel recorded on the same rig over the same session. Each instrument\nran on its own free-running clock; there is no common time base between the\ntwo files and no per-access index anywhere. It exposes two subcommands.\n\n### decode\n\n```\npython3 /app/driver.py decode --capture <bus.csv> --strain <strain.csv> --out <decode.jsonl>\n```\n\nWrites one JSON object per bus access, one object per line, in capture order.\nEach object carries:\n\n    {\"t_us\": <int>, \"cs\": <int>, \"op\": \"R\"|\"W\", \"addr\": <int>,\n     \"revision\": \"C\"|\"D\", \"fields\": {\"<FIELD_NAME>\": <int>, ...}}\n\n`t_us`, `cs`, `op` and `addr` are that access's own values from the capture.\n`revision` is the die revision of that access's card. `fields` maps every\ncanonical field name of the addressed register, as named in the map document,\nto that field's integer code as it sits in the transfer word (apply the map's\ncode scales for physical units). A register that has no defined fields on that\nrevision, and any reserved address, yields `{}`. Each card's revision must be\nestablished from the evidence in the capture itself, not from the probe ID and\nnot from a fixed card-number table.\n\n### excite\n\n```\npython3 /app/driver.py excite --spec <spec.json> --out <writes.json>\n```\n\nThe excitation spec is:\n\n    {\"revision\": \"C\"|\"D\", \"cs\": <int>,\n     \"freq_hz\":  {\"A\": <int>, \"B\": <int>, \"C\": <int>, \"D\": <int>},\n     \"gain\":     {\"A\": <int>, \"B\": <int>, \"C\": <int>, \"D\": <int>},\n     \"phase_deg\":{\"A\": <int>, \"B\": <int>, \"C\": <int>, \"D\": <int>},\n     \"enable\":   {\"A\": <int>, \"B\": <int>, \"C\": <int>, \"D\": <int>}}\n\nWrites:\n\n    {\"writes\": [[<cs>, <addr>, <data>], ...]}\n\nwith integer `cs`, `addr` and `data`, in the order the writes must be applied.\nReplaying those writes in order against a die of the revision named in the\nspec, starting from its power-on defaults, must leave every channel's\nfrequency in Hz, drive level, phase in degrees and enable flag at exactly the\nvalue requested. Use that revision's own register and field placement and the\ncode scales given in the map document, and never write a read-only register.\n\n## Log column conventions\n\nEvery CSV has exactly one header line. Columns are comma separated with no\nquoting and no spaces.\n\n`captures/site_a/bus.csv` - header `t_us,cs,op,addr,data`\n\n| Column | Convention | Meaning                                              |\n|--------|------------|------------------------------------------------------|\n| t_us   | decimal    | microseconds on the bus tool's own clock             |\n| cs     | decimal    | chip select / card number                            |\n| op     | R or W     | R = read transfer, W = write transfer                |\n| addr   | hex, 0xNN  | register address                                     |\n| data   | hex, 0xNNNN| transfer word: value returned on R, value driven on W|\n\n`captures/site_a/strain.csv` - header `t_us,adc`\n\n| Column | Convention | Meaning                                              |\n|--------|------------|------------------------------------------------------|\n| t_us   | decimal    | microseconds on the strain logger's own clock        |\n| adc    | decimal    | strain ADC counts for that sample                    |\n\n## Files staged\n\n    WORKORDER.md                     this order\n    doc/pd440_revC_regmap.md         surviving vendor map document (rev C)\n    doc/revD_addendum.txt            vendor addendum for the later die\n    captures/site_a/bus.csv          post-swap bench bus trace\n    captures/site_a/strain.csv       concurrently recorded strain log\n    excitation_spec.json             example excitation request\n\nThere is no driver, decoder or analysis script on the box, only `python3` and\ncoreutils. Nothing you create under `/app` other than `/app/driver.py` is kept.\n# PD-440 four-channel piezo shaker driver - register map\n\nPart: PD-440\nDocument: PD440-RM-C\nApplies to: PD-440 revision C die\n\n## 1. Bus and registers\n\nThe PD-440 sits on a shared service bus with one chip select per card. A\ntransfer is an 8-bit register address followed by a 16-bit data word,\nmost-significant byte first. A read returns the addressed register; a write\nstores the data word into the addressed register, masked to the bits the\nregister actually implements. Field code scales\n\n| Field     | Width | Scale                                                       |\n|-----------|-------|-------------------------------------------------------------|\n| *_FREQ    | 8 bit | 1 Hz per LSB. Channel frequency in Hz equals the code.      |\n| *_PHASE   | 8 bit | 2 degrees per LSB. Channel phase in degrees equals code x 2.|\n| *_GAIN    | 8 bit | Drive level is the raw code, valid range 1-63. 0 mutes.     |\n| EN_x      | 1 bit | 1 = channel enabled, 0 = channel muted.                     |\n| CLKDIV    | 4 bit | Master clock divider, 0 = divide-by-1.                      |\n| SCRATCH   | 16 bit| Free scratch word, no hardware effect.                      |\n\n## 4. ID word\n\n| Field    | Bits  | Meaning                                  |\n|----------|-------|------------------------------------------|\n| PART_ID  | 15:12 | Part family. 0x5 = PD-440.               |\n| REV      | 11:8  | Die revision. 0x3 = revision C.          |\n| DIE_TRIM | 7:0   | Per-die trim, varies from part to part.  |\n\n## 5. STATUS word\n\nFAULT[15:8] is a latched fault code, 0 = no fault. SEQ_STATE[7:0] is the\nhardware sequencer state and is not software settable.\n\n## 6. Power-on state\n\nEvery writable register powers up as 0x0000, so MASTER reads 0x0000 (all\nchannels disabled) and every field code is 0.\n                         VENDOR PRODUCT NOTICE\n                          PDN-440-D-01  (rev 1)\n                     PD-440 quad piezo driver: rev D die\n\nSCOPE\n  Revision D is a metal-only mask optimisation of the PD-440 rev C die. steps.message: The captures show two different response patterns, but the bus log has no configuration-register readbacks and the strain signal appears to be a noisy level measurement. I’m checking whether the evidence determines the newer die’s full register map; a gain difference alone would not establish its frequency and phase fields.
